newsitem.title: UK: BAe extends losses on Thomson news.
newsitem.headline: BAe extends losses on Thomson news.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc (BA) extended its earlier losses in late trading on Wednesday, amid talk of a deal between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas, and market disappointment over France's suspension of the sale of Thomson.
BA shares slid 29-1/2p or 2.57 percent to 11.20-1/2p stg.

Analysts said a major drag on BAe was the earlier news that the French government had put on hold the privatisation of defence and electronics giant Thomson, for which BAe's partner Lagardere Groupe was a key bidder.

The market also reacted to Tuesday's decision by Boeing Commercial Airplane Group and McDonnell Douglas to collaborate on Boeing wide-body aircraft, a move expected to put pressure on Airbus Industrie. BAe is an Airbus partner.
Analysts said while both factors were significant, the Thomson news had had more impact.
The French Finance Ministry said earlier it suspended the Thomson sale because favoured-bidder Lagardere's plans to sell off a multimedia division had been blocked.
One industry analyst said speculation about a possible Boeing-McDonnell Douglas link-up was likely to have a less immediate effect on BAe.

"BAe was more hopeful of benefits from the Thomson privatisation than of Airbus joining forces with McDonnell Douglas," said one analyst, adding that the Boeing deal could even eventually boost BAe's market share.
Boeing President Ron Woodward earlier played down talk of a merger with McDonnell Douglas, saying he first wanted to get the cooperation programme running.

Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, BAe, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA of Spain. -- Catherine Bremer, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
